questions.question: How sharp is the main subject?

real_s1.explanation: The unit responds to vehicles and wading birds (and similar elongated subjects) seen in side view facing or pointing right, framed at medium size (filling a quarter to three quarters of the photo), sharp, and photographed level. It is weaker for left-facing subjects, for scenes without a single clear subject, and for blurry or tilted shots.

real_s2.explanation: The unit responds to vehicles and wading birds shown side-on, especially facing right. It is most active when one clear, sharp main subject sits in the middle of the frame, fills a moderate share of it (a quarter to three quarters), and is shown in level, ordinary lighting. Its preference for rightward facing over leftward facing is unusual and not shared by its similar units. Its preference for sharp over slightly blurry subjects also looks specific to it. Photos with no single main subject, blur or tilt lower its activity.

real_s3.explanation: The unit responds to vehicles and wading birds, the classes it is most active on. Within those classes it is most active when a single, sharp, level main subject faces or points to the right and fills a moderate share of the frame, from a quarter to three quarters. It is weakest on photos with no single main subject, with left-facing subjects, with blurry subjects and with tilted horizons. The right-versus-left facing preference is the most distinctive feature, because the similar units show it only weakly.

null_s1.explanation: The unit responds to vehicles (cars, vans, trucks, buses) and shorebirds. Within those classes it is somewhat more active when the subject is large and fills the frame (more than three quarters, often partly cut off) and well lit. It is also more active when the photo has a noticeable colour tint, warm or cool, and when the main lines are level rather than tilted. None of the effects is strong; no row reaches the 95th percentile.

null_s2.explanation: The unit responds to vehicles (cars, vans, trucks, buses) and shorebirds. Within those classes it is somewhat more active when the subject is large and fills the frame. It also responds more to photos with a noticeable color tint, especially a warm one, to brightly lit subjects, and to level rather than tilted compositions. All effects are modest; no row reaches the 95th percentile. The tint and level-horizon preferences are the most distinctive, though one similar unit partly shares each.

null_s3.explanation: The unit responds mostly to vehicles (vans, buses, emergency trucks, cars, grilles) and some wading shorebirds. Within those classes, the composition effects are weak and none reach the 95th percentile. The unit leans toward large subjects that fill most of the frame and are partly cut off. It also leans toward photos with a color tint (warm or cool) over neutral ones, toward a brightly lit single subject, and toward level lines over tilted ones. The tilt and warm-tint effects are partly shared with the similar units. Subject size, cool tint and bright lighting look more particular to this unit.
